decisions.reason: As a close extension of the existing interiors range introduced only recently, it is likely to be retained because the firm appears to have enough slack in a growing market to give such adjacent products more time unless results clearly disappoint.

This premium hand-knotted wool-silk carpet is somewhat more niche and may face a higher aspiration threshold, but the firm's design-led positioning and broad offer make continued retention more likely than withdrawal after just one year.
Because it is another close-to-core carpet addition in a firm with a broad catalog, management would likely keep it while monitoring performance rather than trigger problemistic search immediately.
The corner bench builds directly on the firm's established furniture competence, so in the absence of signs of failure it likely meets or nearly meets aspirations and is worth keeping on the market.

This low-pile carpet sits near the firm's existing offer and benefits from portfolio fit, so boundedly rational management would usually continue it unless early sales clearly fell short of comparable products.

A swivel shell chair line with several models is closely aligned with the firm's workplace and public-interior direction, making retention most likely because it reflects a more committed product-family investment.
